name: fanbasis
one_liner: Commas (formerly FanBasis) is a payments/checkout and payouts platform for creators and digital-product sellers, positioned as a Stripe alternative with embedded checkout, subscriptions, and BNPL.
auto_notes: pass1/pass2 disagree on access (self_serve_free vs partner_gated)
formula verdict red, model said yellow

evidence.quote: Sign in to access API Docs
Embedded checkouts, multi-rail payouts, APIs and SDKs. Everything you'd replace Stripe with, plus BNPL, recovery and lower effective rates.

notes: FanBasis has rebranded to "Commas" — fanbasis.com and www.fanbasis.com both 301-redirect to commas.com. The company positions itself as a Stripe-alternative payments/checkout platform for creators, with "APIs and SDKs" mentioned in enterprise-facing marketing copy on commas.com. An API reference exists (commasdocs.com / apidocs.fan / fbnewapi.netlify.app all resolve to the same Mintlify-style doc site), but it is a JS-rendered SPA that could not be fully read via fetch (returned only "Commas API Reference" placeholder text), so specific auth-flow and endpoint-count details could not be verified with verbatim quotes. A separate docs subdomain, dev-docs.fanbasis.com ("FanBasis API Docsv3"), is password-gated behind a login screen ("Sign in to access API Docs"), indicating documentation/API access is not fully open to the public. Community references (npm @fanbasis/checkout-sdk, unverified secondary summaries) suggest API keys are created via an "Account > API Keys" dashboard section and SDKs exist for Node/Python/PHP/Ruby, but these were not confirmed against a primary source page within the search/fetch budget. Given the enterprise-sales framing ("Everything you'd replace Stripe with") and gated docs, classified as partner_gated/yellow with low-moderate confidence — a follow-up pass with a JS-rendering fetch (or manual browsing of commasdocs.com) is recommended to confirm auth method details and endpoint breadth.
